commenter_information.stakeholder_type: Technology Vendor / Health IT Convener / Other
commenter_information.credentials_or_expertise_mentioned: Non-profit public-private collaborative advancing interoperability; supports RSNA Image Share Validation Program and Interoperability Matters Cooperative; ONC-selected Recognized Coordinating Entity for TEFCA; experience with nationwide health information exchange and federated directory governance.

executive_summary: The Sequoia Project generally supports CMS efforts to align API requirements with ONC-adopted unexpired standards, improve payer endpoint discovery, and move toward FHIR-based prior authorization. It recommends a practical transition that accounts for version management, implementation maturity, directory governance, endpoint validation, and trusted exchange infrastructure, while urging CMS to leverage TEFCA for event notifications and resiliency.

standards_referenced: FAST National Directory of Healthcare Providers & Services (NDH) Endpoint Profile
Da Vinci Clinical Data Exchange (CDex) IG

detailed_positions.rationale: Alignment reduces implementation variation and promotes consistency across federal interoperability initiatives.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Finalize alignment with ONC-adopted unexpired standards and continue coordination across federal interoperability programs.

detailed_positions.topic: Payer API endpoint reporting and directory strategy
detailed_positions.rationale: Endpoint discovery is necessary for scalable interoperability, but directories require governance, validation, lifecycle management, and trust processes over time.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Align endpoint reporting with existing directory standards, including NDH, National Provider Directory efforts, and structured reporting mechanisms; provide implementation guidance, verification methods, and adequate time if requirements differ from existing approaches.

detailed_positions.topic: FHIR-based prior authorization as HIPAA standard
detailed_positions.rationale: FHIR prior authorization can improve automation, but the standards may not yet convey all information needed for all prior authorization scenarios and require directory/trust infrastructure.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Use a phased, practical transition; assess CDex and other FHIR approaches in real-world use before broad mandates; ensure FHIR can support the full range of clinical information needed.

detailed_positions.rationale: TEFCA provides national governance, directory, and connectivity infrastructure that could improve delivery to authorized recipients, although event notifications are not an initial TEFCA Exchange use case.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Encourage and incentivize regulated providers and payers to participate in TEFCA and evaluate event notifications as a future TEFCA exchange scenario.

detailed_positions.rationale: A network-of-networks approach can reduce reliance on a single pathway and support continuity of information sharing during disruptions.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Use TEFCA governance and trusted nationwide exchange infrastructure as part of resiliency strategy.

solicitation_responses.summary: Supports requiring alignment with unexpired ONC-adopted standards and coordinated version management.
Supports payer endpoint reporting but urges structured formats, alignment with NDH and national directory efforts, validation, governance, and lifecycle guidance.

Supports long-term FHIR-based prior authorization but urges phased implementation, evaluation of CDex maturity, directory/trust infrastructure, and confirmation that FHIR can carry needed clinical information.
Responds to RFIs on event notifications and resiliency by recommending TEFCA participation, future TEFCA event-notification use cases, and network-of-networks resiliency planning.

recommendations: Finalize alignment with ONC-adopted unexpired standards.
Align endpoint reporting with existing directory standards and reporting mechanisms.
Consider NDH Endpoint Profile and National Provider Directory initiatives for endpoint discovery.
Provide guidance on endpoint verification, automated validation, evidence, third-party validation, governance, and lifecycle management.
Adopt a phased and practical transition to FHIR-based prior authorization and evaluate CDex maturity before broad requirements.
Encourage payer and provider participation in TEFCA and evaluate event notifications as a future TEFCA exchange scenario.
Use trusted nationwide exchange and federated directories to support healthcare resiliency.

primary_concerns: Endpoint directories can become stale without governance and maintenance.
A 60-day implementation window may be insufficient if CMS changes reporting approaches.
FHIR prior authorization standards may not yet support all clinical information needed.
FHIR implementation maturity and version management need attention.
potential_negative_impacts_cited: Implementation burden, duplicative directory efforts, unreliable endpoint information, incomplete prior authorization information exchange.
implementation_barriers_mentioned: Directory validation, endpoint lifecycle management, trust infrastructure, standards maturity, version management, industry readiness.

supporting_evidence.studies_or_research_referenced: No studies cited; relies on Sequoia experience operating TEFCA-related federated directory and nationwide exchange infrastructure.
examples_provided: TEFCA federated directory model for QHINs, Participants, and Subparticipants.
FAST NDH Endpoint Profile as a possible reporting format.

impact_assessment.economic_implications: Potential burden reduction through directory alignment and reduced duplicative implementation; possible added implementation cost if reporting requirements diverge or are rushed.
impact_assessment.technical_feasibility: Feasible with sufficient guidance, version management, endpoint validation, and trusted directory infrastructure.
impact_assessment.patient_care_impact: Improved endpoint discovery and trusted exchange could support more reliable prior authorization, event notification, and care coordination.

key_quotes: CMS should prioritize a phased and practical transition that balances innovation with implementation readiness.
Endpoint directories are not static compliance registries.
The success of FHIR-based prior authorization will depend not only on the standards themselves, but also on the directory, discovery, and trust infrastructure that enables reliable exchange.
Greater participation in TEFCA will strengthen the network effects necessary to support scalable care coordination and notification use cases.
